summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate blocked it because the custom steady experiment has no blocks and no power_w object, so input validity failed. The selected scenario is thermal-aware redundant-TSV insertion in a 4x4x4 (64-core) 3D-NoC (Figure 9, Section IV-F). Its reported outcome is system MTTF relative to a target at Tref, derived from HotSpot 6.0 router temperatures and Black's model. It is not a temperature field. No Studio thermal result exists, and the experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so there is no transient trace either. comparison_valid is false, and no numerical comparison with the paper's normalized MTTF or redundancy results is made. Nothing here replicates or checks the paper's claim, for example that the no-redundancy 10:0 case falls below 50% of target MTTF. Qualitatively, the paper's logic is that hotter routers have higher fault rates and so receive more redundant TSVs. That is a reliability argument layered on a 3D thermal solve, and it cannot be tested here. A 2D steady Studio model could at best show lateral hotspot sensitivity within one layer. It would not reflect inter-layer coupling, TSV thermal effects, or the Black's-model chain. The gate also lists unresolved evidence-locator, asset-pinning and adversarial-review checks, so the extraction is unverified. The linked references (NanGate, FreePDK3D45, PARSEC, HotSpot 6.0 report, JPL text) are citations, not thermal input files.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated thermal output of any kind.
The 2D screening verdict is not_2d_applicable, and comparison_valid is false, so no numerical comparison with the paper is made.

The extracted experiment is empty (floorplan [] and power_w {}). The paper gives no block names, coordinates, dimensions or per-block watts, and total power must not be split without a published rule.

The paper's observable is normalized system MTTF relative to Tref, not temperature. Black's-model parameters (Ea, J, n), absolute Tref and theta1/theta2 values are not given, and Figure 9 values are not digitized.
The scenario is a 4-layer 3D stack with TSV vertical links. A steady 2D model cannot represent inter-layer coupling or TSV thermal effects.

The HotSpot 6.0 layer stack, package, heat sink, ambient and boundary conditions are unspecified, so Studio defaults would define a different scenario. No transient behaviour is reported, and a custom steady run would have no transient trace.
The optimizer (grid search over fault-rate thresholds) and the IaSiG hardware TSV fault detector are reliability mechanisms with no thermal-controller counterpart in Studio.

The evidence entries lack valid page or pinned-asset locators, the linked assets are unpinned reference URLs, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved. The extracted claims are therefore unverified.
This assessment does not claim exact replication of the paper.
